title: Risk assessment of N-nitrosamines in food
authors: EFSA Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain (CONTAM), Schrenk D, Bignami M, Bodin L, Chipman JK, del Mazo J, et al.
funder: European Food Safety Authority; requestor: European Commission (Question number EFSA-Q-2020-00665).
authorConflicts: Declarations of interest of contributing experts are available on request from EFSA; not read.
result: Assessment of 10 carcinogenic N-nitrosamines occurring in food (NDMA, NMEA, NDEA, NDPA, NDBA, NMA, NSAR, NMOR, NPIP, NPYR), assumed equally potent; BMDL10 10 μg/kg body weight per day from rat liver tumours induced by NDEA. Exposure 0 to 208.9 ng/kg body weight per day across surveys, age groups and scenarios. Meat and meat products were the main contributing food category, 7 to 100% of exposure across surveys excluding cooked unprocessed meat and fish and 20 to 99% including them. Margins of exposure at the 95th percentile 3337 to 48; highly likely (98 to 100% certain) to be below 10,000 for all age groups, which raises a health concern.
